# Billing System Migration Rollout Plan
## 40,000 Users — Legacy → New Billing System (Dual-Run Supported)

## Overview

Both billing systems can run concurrently, which allows a gradual, reversible migration rather than a hard cutover. Users are moved in increasing batches, with validation gates between phases. The old system stays live in read/write parity mode until well after the final user batch is confirmed stable.

---

## Phase 1: Pilot (5% of users — 2,000 users)

**Entry criterion:** New billing system has passed full integration testing in staging, including invoice generation, payment capture, tax calculation, and dunning workflows against a shadow copy of production data; rollback procedure has been tested end-to-end at least once.

- Select users from low-risk segments: internal/employee accounts, free-tier or low-ARPU users, and opted-in beta testers.
- Run both systems in parallel for this cohort; new system is authoritative, old system continues shadow billing for reconciliation.
- Manual review of every invoice and payment discrepancy during this phase.
- Duration: minimum 2 full billing cycles before advancing.

## Phase 2: Expansion (30% of users — 12,000 users)

**Entry criterion:** Phase 1 cohort shows invoice accuracy ≥ 99.9%, zero unresolved payment-processing incidents, and reconciliation discrepancies fully explained and closed for both completed billing cycles.

- Broaden to a representative cross-section of plan types, geographies, and payment methods (cards, ACH, wallets, invoiced enterprise).
- Automated reconciliation between old and new systems runs continuously; alerts route to on-call.
- Support team fully trained and staffed for elevated ticket volume.
- Duration: minimum 1 full billing cycle before advancing.

## Phase 3: General Availability (65% of users — 26,000 users, remaining balance)

**Entry criterion:** Phase 2 shows invoice accuracy ≥ 99.95%, payment failure rate delta vs. old system ≤ 0.1 percentage points, and support ticket volume attributable to migration trending flat or down over the prior cycle.

- Migrate all remaining users, including highest-complexity enterprise/custom-contract accounts last, in sub-batches (e.g., 4 waves of ~6,500) rather than one bulk cutover.
- Old system remains live in parallel, read-write, for reconciliation and fallback for at least one full billing cycle after the last wave completes.
- **Decommissioning of the old billing system is explicitly out of scope for Phase 3 and is deferred to a separate, subsequent Phase 4 (post-migration stabilization and sunset), which does not begin until the final Phase 3 wave has completed at least one clean billing cycle with no rollback events.**

---

## Risks

RISK: Duplicate or double charges when both systems process the same billing event | Implement idempotency keys and a single source-of-truth flag per account before enabling writes in the new system | Payments Engineering Lead
RISK: Data drift between old and new customer/payment records during dual-run causes reconciliation to silently diverge | Run automated hourly reconciliation jobs with alerting on any mismatch above threshold, plus daily manual spot-checks | Data Integrity Team
RISK: Enterprise customers on custom contract terms are migrated incorrectly, causing invoicing disputes | Migrate enterprise/custom-contract accounts last, in small manual-reviewed sub-batches, with account manager sign-off per account | Enterprise Billing Owner
RISK: Rollback is attempted too late because no clear halt criteria exist | Define and monitor numeric halt thresholds (see below) with automatic pause of further migration batches when breached | Migration Program Manager

---

## Halt / Rollback Metric

**If invoice error rate for any active phase exceeds 0.5% of invoices generated in a rolling 24-hour window, halt all further batch migrations immediately, freeze the current cohort, and initiate rollback review before resuming.**

Additional supporting thresholds:
- Payment failure rate increase > 0.2 percentage points vs. old-system baseline for the same cohort → halt.
- Reconciliation discrepancy backlog > 50 open items unresolved for > 48 hours → halt.

---

PHASES: 3
